Fable-Opus-Unit: bank-demo-fleet-pipeline-p2g/interim-audit-2026-08-20
Fable-Opus-Timeout-Minutes: 30

## Goal

READ-ONLY interim audit of goal bank-demo-fleet-pipeline against its ORACLE, at HEAD (6f1acac), in the T042/T999 house style (read `docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/goal.md` — the oracle definition, the T042 verdict section, and today's decision boxes — plus `notes/T042-reaudit.md` for the audit discipline). Produce ONE file: `docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/notes/interim-audit-2026-08-20.md`. Every claim carries its evidence path; every number is read from disk during this audit, never quoted from notes.

The oracle has two halves, both required. Audit each:

**Half 1 — the command.** One command, clean-checkout-runnable, on an unseen app, interventionCount 0. Verify at HEAD: read the current flame record (9/9? count 0? bounded?), the three NEW proven records from today (coverview, cra-redux, your-spotify — each 9/9, count 0, through which policies), and state what "unseen app" evidence exists (which of the proven four were first-invocation runs on apps the pipeline had never proven). Note what is NOT re-verified here (you run nothing — this audit reads; the clean-checkout re-run is T042's sealed result plus today's fresh-lane runs).

**Half 2 — coverage + capability above baseline.** Read `evidence/trust/current/coverage-report.json`: totals vs the sealed baseline (proven 10 sealed / 8-of-58 capability at goal start). State the movement: proven 14 (which 4 by run-record derivation), applications 29, every non-proven row's code (list the distinct codes with counts). Read `capability-coverage.json` + the coverage report's capabilities block: 8/51/59, plus the ONE derived proof (react-cra-vite-adapter, flame). Verdict per conjunct: STRICTLY ABOVE baseline or not, with the honest note that cross-proven 8 has not moved (denominator grew, one capability's proofs grew).

**The gap map.** What stands between HEAD and the goal's full outcome, each item with its owner: (a) T044's five frozen items (quote the brief's enumeration, note items 1-2 proven sufficient by u1c, item 4 blocking the first Angular build crossing at any cell); (b) consent ruling (four apps + the ionic precedent); (c) foreign-lockfile proven-reachability; (d) the still-unanswered lane-wide question (fuxa stopped short); (e) witness for Angular (never reached). Then the demo-readiness statement against the ORIGINAL ask (a top-10 US bank, production-ready migration of older React and Angular apps): what a bank's auditor would see today (the honest inventory: react line proven end-to-end 4 apps with named-policy admission; angular line proven to 7/9 with every wall named and priced), and what they would NOT yet see.

**Audit integrity checks** (run, read-only): `npm run trust:verify -- --offline`; `node --experimental-strip-types packages/cli/src/cli.ts report:coverage --offline --verify-only`; the census verify-only; the freeze composite. Record their outputs verbatim in the note. If ANY disagrees with what the notes claim, that discrepancy IS the audit's headline.

Do NOT declare full_outcome_complete — it is not, and the note must say which conjuncts hold and which wait.

## File contract

- `docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/notes/interim-audit-2026-08-20.md`

## Forbidden moves

- Read-only apart from the single note; no pipeline runs, no regeneration, no git state commands. Why: an audit that changes what it audits is not an audit.

## Verification

```verify
test -f docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/notes/interim-audit-2026-08-20.md && wc -l < docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/notes/interim-audit-2026-08-20.md
git diff --quiet HEAD -- packages evidence && echo NOTHING-TOUCHED
npm run trust:verify -- --offline
```

## Blocked permission

If any integrity check contradicts the published record in a way that needs adjudication before the audit can state a verdict, return status "blocked" with the discrepancy in open_questions instead of writing around it.

# One-Command Migration + Coverage Breadth

## Objective

Make `versionless migrate <app>` a single unattended command that runs from invocation to a
coverage report with **zero manual steps** — no hand-authored journeys, no per-app receipt
modules, no human opening files to check the migration worked — and then use that command to
grind as many additional real React and Angular apps through the pipeline as it will chew,
widening proven coverage so that when the owner runs it live on a top-10 US bank's own repo,
their apps largely just work.

Two things must become true, in this order, because the first is what makes the second
affordable:

1. **One command, end to end.** Today the full pipeline lives in fixture code and the operator
   `migrate` emits a non-installable tree (spike C). Every remaining manual stage —
   ingest, license-at-pin, era-cell provisioning, install/build, witness journey authoring,
   receipt module authoring — becomes a stage of one command that ends in a coverage report.
2. **Coverage breadth.** With authoring cost removed, run real React and Angular apps through
   that command continuously. Every app either raises proven coverage or emits a *named,
   countable, honest refusal* that becomes the next admission backlog item.

## Original Request

"use fable opus cockpit, goal prep, and 15m /loop to figure out where to continue versionless,
so that I can have it ready to show a large top 10 US bank and it being production ready for
doing a migration of older React and Angular apps"

Clarified by the owner during intake:

> "the actual demo to them will be when I do their repo. YOUR demos / equivalent will be more
> React and Angular apps to improve coverage as much as possible so that their apps transform
> would largely work. And it needs to be fully end to end where from command to done where it
> gives you the coverage report. We can't be having to expect someone manually check each file
> etc. part of the migration no, it should be as easy as versionless migrate or something"

## Intake Summary

- Input shape: `existing_plan` — the sealed owner decision brief
  (`docs/goals/next-tranche-strategy/notes/owner-decision-brief.md`) is a receipt-backed,
  audited plan. It is preserved as facts below and validated by T001 against the owner's
  clarified outcome, which it does not fully price.
- Audience: the owner (operator on stage), and downstream a top-10 US bank's migration team.
- Authority: `approved` — owner directed the tranche and named the sequencing constraint.
- Proof type: `demo` + `metric` — an unattended command run, and a coverage number that moves.
- Completion proof: a clean-checkout run of the single command against an app the pipeline has
  never handled, completing unattended to a coverage report, with a human-intervention count of
  zero; plus a strictly increased proven-app count and capability matrix versus the sealed
  baseline.
- Goal oracle: see below.
- Likely misfire: **building a beautiful staged demo instead of coverage.** The board could
  produce a polished one-command run over the existing fixture corpus, report success, and
  leave the bank's actual apps just as likely to fail. The command is the *enabler*; the
  coverage number is the product. A tranche that automates the pipeline and grinds no new apps
  has not met the outcome. The second misfire is **silent manual residue** — a stage that
  "works" because a human quietly does one step; T008 exists to catch exactly that.
- Blind spots considered:
  - "Zero manual steps" must be *measured*, not asserted. Hence an explicit intervention count.
  - Coverage breadth is bounded by admission, not by throughput (machine time is ~0.8 ms/app).
    Refusals, not slowness, are what cap the number — so refusals must be named and countable.
  - Honest-outcome vocabulary must survive automation: a synthesized journey that cannot reach
    a surface must still emit a bounded string, never a generic pass. Automation must not
    become a way to launder overclaim.
  - The bank's repo is unseen and unseeable in advance. The only defence is breadth plus
    legible refusal — an app that fails must fail with a named reason on stage, not a crash.
- Existing plan facts (preserved from the sealed brief, to validate not to obey):
  - Sealed baseline: 6/6 React + 4/4 Angular derived matrix; React holdout `passed` (76f0b5bd);
    Angular holdout `witness-passed-on-bounded-anonymous-catalog-surface` (fb921b46 — the
    bounded string is part of the claim); freeze `27741d9c`; three permanent REDs; 8
    capabilities cross-proven in-matrix, 50 experimental out.
  - Declared pre-Ivy boundary: "pre-Ivy-only dependencies (no published Ivy successor) in active
    application use ⇒ unsupported at the Angular 16 target cell" (observed 5-of-6, population
    statement). It stays true *for the 16 cell*; a 13 cell earns its own evidence.
  - Spike A: ngcc 12/13 feasible; honest cell **Angular 13.4.0 / Node 16**, real ngcc, rxjs 6.
    One library already Ivy, one back-compiles clean, one needs `-p module main`

intervention on an unseen app. Phase 2 opens admission (Angular 13 cell; ejected-CRA if the
census justifies it) and then grinds real apps through the command until the coverage report's

## Non-Negotiable Constraints

- **Zero manual steps is the acceptance bar, and it is counted.** Any stage that still needs a
  human is either automated or explicitly recorded as an open intervention in the receipt. Do
  not describe a pipeline as end-to-end while a human step remains.
- **Automation must not launder overclaim.** Synthesized journeys inherit the same measured-pins
  and bounded-outcome vocabulary as hand-authored ones. An unreachable surface yields a bounded
  string, never a generic pass. Existing bounded claims are quoted verbatim, never restated more
  generally.
- **Refusals must be named and countable.** An app the pipeline cannot handle must exit with a
  specific admission string that a report can tally. A crash, a hang, or a non-installable tree
  is a defect, not a refusal.
- **Freeze discipline.** Phase 2's supersession is authorized, chain-recorded, single, and
  boundary amendments are append-only. The pre-Ivy boundary statement stays true for the 16 cell.
- **Witness stays serialized per host** (determinism-under-load finding). Operator stages may
  parallelize.
- **Prune-after-receipt is permitted** (proven safe); the evidence tree is the disk floor.
- Coverage claims stay derivation-guarded — the enterprise report and capability matrix remain
  offline-verifiable, and the payment/locality scans (`successfulNonLoopback: 0`) still gate.

a whole pipeline stage folded into the command, a whole era cell, or a whole coverage batch. It
is not one helper, one contract file, or one doc note.

work goes in one package and is reviewed as a whole.

3. **T027's named blind spot stands, and T023/T028/T029 only partly closed it.** The pipeline now
   READS what an operator would have pre-declared (revision from the consent journal; node major
   from CI/Dockerfile/volta/.tool-versions), which is the right fix and is real progress. But the
   flame proof still required three fleet-wide policies pre-declared in the first invocation
   (`--allow-remote-tarballs --allow-install-scripts --allow-peer-conflicts`), each scoring zero.
   That is defensible as one recorded operator decision — the T008 ruling permits it — but it is not
   "no declarations".

**And one residue nobody named**, which is the most serious finding in this audit — see §4.

---

## 4. Honesty audit

**Bounded-string discipline: HOLDS.** Greps across `coverage-report.{json,md}`, `report.md`,
`enterprise-report.md` and the runbook found no restatement. Every occurrence carries the verbatim
string plus its surface limits ("identity is out of surface … the SignalR hub was never reached"),
"a pass on a bounded surface and not a generic pass", "counted in no lineage numerator", and the
permanent install RED under `f1a63359` retained beside the later result. `assertEnterpriseSurfaceHonesty`
still gates (`packages/trust/src/enterprise.ts:944`, invoked from `coverage-report.ts:612` and
`enterprise.ts:1078`); `report:coverage --offline --verify-only` exits 0 in the working tree.
**This is the strongest part of the tranche.**

All 18 non-sample hooks in `.git/hooks/` were overwritten on that date and every one sources

`git checkout --`), printing `cd: .versionless/work/react-mycrypto/baseline/: No such file or
directory`.

An acquired third-party application's `postinstall`, run under the fleet-wide
`--allow-install-scripts` policy, **escaped its lane and wrote to the host repository's git hooks.**

carried this as "the pre-commit hook skipping for want of yarn" — that framing understates it by a
wide margin. Sandboxing the install stage is a release blocker.

the defect and its own remedy, in two files, disagreeing about one file format.** The lane half

Naming this precisely matters for the T044 case because of what it is *not*: it is not a cell
rewrite, not an ETARGET, not owner-gated, and not 13-specific. It fires on the **default 16
path**, on a post-Ivy Angular 14 application, at plan, before any cell rewrite is composed.

### 18.1.2 What fuxa did and did not settle about the standing question

The packet's strategic question was whether the Angular build wall is 13-cell-specific or
lane-wide. **Fuxa does not answer it, and the honest record is that it could not: it never
reached `build`.** It stopped two stages earlier, at plan, on a wall nobody had predicted. What it
did establish, and what is new:

1. The default 16 path is reachable and was taken — `angular-16-browser-builder`, runtime
   provisioned, era `not-read`. That much of the screen's post-Ivy reading is now measured rather
   than derived.
2. There is a **second Angular wall, upstream of the build wall and independent of the 13 cell**,
   which no prior unit had seen because every prior Angular candidate carried a strict-JSON
   tsconfig.
3. **No Angular application has still ever crossed `run`'s build stage.** T043-b's statement
   stands, and this unit moved neither of the two applications that could have tested it to the
   stage that would have.

The cheapest next test of the original question is therefore *still* an Angular application on
the 16 path — but one whose `tsconfig.json` parses strictly. That is now a one-line pre-read any
future screen can take (`JSON.parse` the frontend root's `tsconfig.json`), and this unit took it
for `angular-contacts` before spending its run (§18.5).

version: 2

goal:
  title: "One-Command Migration + Coverage Breadth"
  slug: "bank-demo-fleet-pipeline"
  kind: existing_plan
  tranche: "Phase 1 folds every manual stage into one unattended command ending in a coverage report (measured by a zero human-intervention count on an unseen app). Phase 2 opens admission (Angular 13 cell, ejected-CRA if the census justifies) and grinds real React/Angular apps through that command until the coverage report's numbers stop moving cheaply. Continuous execution until both oracle halves hold."
  status: active
  oracle:
    signal: "In a clean checkout, one command run against a real React or Angular app the pipeline has never handled completes unattended - no human edits a file, authors a journey, writes a receipt module, or inspects output to decide the result - and ends in a coverage report that either records the app as newly proven or names a countable refusal reason."
    cadence: "after each Worker package and at final audit"
    final_proof: "Two receipts, both required. (1) Command half: a clean-checkout run on an unseen app with a recorded human-intervention count of zero. (2) Coverage half: the coverage report's proven-app count and capability matrix strictly above the sealed baseline (6/6 React + 4/4 Angular derived matrix, 8 capabilities cross-proven in-matrix), with every non-admitted app carrying a named countable refusal string."
  intake:
    original_request: "use fable opus cockpit, goal prep, and 15m /loop to figure out where to continue versionless, so that I can have it ready to show a large top 10 US bank and it being production ready for doing a migration of older React and Angular apps"
    interpreted_outcome: "Make `versionless migrate <app>` a single unattended command from invocation to coverage report with zero manual steps, then use it to widen proven React/Angular coverage so an unseen bank repo largely just works when the owner runs it live."
    input_shape: existing_plan
    audience: "Owner (operator running the live demo); downstream a top-10 US bank migration team"
    authority: approved
    proof_type: demo
    completion_proof: "Clean-checkout unattended run on a never-handled app with intervention count zero, plus coverage report numbers strictly above the sealed baseline."
    likely_misfire: "Building a polished staged demo over the existing fixture corpus instead of moving coverage. The command is the enabler; the coverage number is the product. Second misfire: silent manual residue - a stage that only 'works' because a human quietly does one step."
    blind_spots_considered:
      - "Zero manual steps must be counted, not asserted - hence an explicit human-intervention count as a gate (T008)."
      - "Coverage breadth is capped by admission, not throughput (0.8 ms/app). Refusals are the real ceiling, so they must be named and countable."
      - "Automation must not launder overclaim: synthesized journeys inherit measured-pins and bounded-outcome vocabulary; unreachable surfaces yield bounded strings, never generic passes."
      - "The bank's repo is unseeable in advance. The only defence is breadth plus legible refusal - failing with a named reason on stage beats crashing."
      - "Era cells need x64/Rosetta host capacity (node-sass has no arm64 binding at any Node); a coverage grind can be blocked by host pool, not by code."
    existing_plan_facts:
      - "Source: docs/goals/next-tranche-strategy/notes/owner-decision-brief.md (sealed, receipt-backed, T999-audited). Preserved as facts; validated by T001 against the owner's clarified outcome, which the brief does not fully price."
      - "Sealed baseline: derived 6/6 React + 4/4 Angular matrix; React holdout passed (receipt 76f0b5bd); Angular holdout 'witness-passed-on-bounded-anonymous-catalog-surface' (receipt fb921b46 - the bounded string is part of the claim); freeze 27741d9c; three permanent REDs; 8 capabilities cross-proven in-matrix, 50 experimental out."
      - "Declared pre-Ivy boundary: 'pre-Ivy-only dependencies (no published Ivy successor) in active application use => unsupported at the Angular 16 target cell' (observed 5-of-6, population statement). Stays true for the 16 cell; a 13 cell earns its own evidence."
      - "Spike A: ngcc 12/13 feasible. Honest cell Angular 13.4.0 / Node 16, real ngcc, rxjs 6. One library already Ivy, one back-compiles clean, one needs '-p module main' (exit-0-with-broken-typing trap documented). Est ~25-35 units. Moves ~25 -> ~125+ of the ~150-app Angular fleet."
      - "Spike B: 0.8 ms/app median, whole fleet ~6s. Prune-after-receipt safe (offline verify passes with work dir absent). Operator stages parallelizable; witness must stay serialized (determinism-under-load)."
      - "Spike C: unreached, not refuted - hit admission walls first. Ejected-CRA / vendored-webpack trees are refused by the frozen adapter; operator 'migrate' emits a non-installable tree; the full pipeline lives in fixture code."
      - "Authoring is the cost: witness journeys/calibration were ~48% of the largest tranche's units. Journey synthesis from an app's own e2e suite is precedented (cypress-rwa holdout)."
      - "Carried tranche-two commitments: the ngcc 12/13 cell, and the format epoch (249 non-canonical files, 82 freeze-locked) riding the same freeze supersession (T003 ruling)."
      - "Flagged one-liner: the fable-opus packet parser mishandles quote-wrapped contract bullets."
      - "Ledger effort baselines: React vertical 9-10u; Angular 10u; chase 4-7u; operator CLI 2u (.fable-opus/runs/*/ledger.jsonl)."

  pm_owns_state: true
  one_active_task: true
  max_write_workers: 1
  no_implementation_without_worker_or_pm_task: true
  no_completion_without_judge_or_pm_audit: true
  planning_is_not_completion: true
  queued_required_worker_blocks_completion: true
  continuous_until_full_outcome: true
  missing_input_or_credentials_do_not_stop_goal: true

## 5. Consent: what the record actually contains (recorded, not decided)

Owner decision 3 is pending and this unit does not touch it. But the screen turned up a third
data point that neither §14.5 of T012 nor the T010 ruling line records, and it is the most
directly on-point of the three:

`evidence/ingests/angular-ionic-conference/` — acquired **under `VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10`
itself**, `networkMode: "consented"`, for a repository whose licence at the pin is Apache-2.0.
The transaction completed: the tag resolved, two archives were byte-identical, every file
reconciled blob-for-blob. And then `admission.json` records `decision: "not-admitted"`, because —
verbatim —

> "The first admission gate — MIT LICENSE file content at the exact pinned revision — fails."

and `source.json` records `result: "source-bound-not-admitted"` with:

> "Bound bytes are not an admission."

So the three facts now on the table, all recorded rather than reconciled:

1. `react-your-spotify-1-5-0` (GPL-3.0) is **in the corpus**, acquired under the grant, and its
   root `LICENSE` on disk is the GPL v3 text. `acquire.ts` applies no SPDX filter.
2. The four T6xx react applications each got their **own** per-application grant, which is what
   one does when the corpus grant does not reach.
3. `angular-ionic-conference` shows the grant being used to **fetch** a non-MIT source and the
   MIT test being applied at **admission**, not at acquisition — a third position distinct from
   both of the above, and the only one where a worker wrote down the reasoning at the time.

Fact 3 is the one that would change the shape of the ruling if it went unmentioned: the question
may not be "does the grant reach non-MIT source" but "at which gate does MIT bind — the socket or
the admission". Not decided here. Recorded, with paths, so the ruling is made on the whole record.

One correction the ruling should carry: **it names four applications; three is the honest number.**
Strapi is excluded on its own licence terms under either branch (§2.9), and `saleor-dashboard`'s
consent would buy a refusal at plan rather than a proven row (§2.8). And it should gain one:
`angular-kubernetes-dashboard` is Apache-2.0 and its shipped re-acquire path is consent-blocked
in exactly the same way (§2.15).

---

## 6. Finding: no published coverage row claims a framework its manifest contradicts

Item 5 of this unit's packet. Every one of the 24 rows in
`evidence/trust/current/coverage-report.json` was checked against the reading its own basis
allows:

- The 9 `run-record` rows that are not sealed (`react-verdaccio-v4-12-2`, `react-cra-redux-1a06509b`,
  `react-your-spotify-1-5-0`, `react-colorme-2019-06-06`, `react-ant-design-pro-v5-2-0`,
  `react-mycrypto`, `react-antd-admin-template-v2-0-0`, `angular2-hn`,
  `angular-kubernetes-dashboard`) were re-read from their trees on disk. **Every `framework` field
  matches the manifest at the pin.** Spot readings: colorme `react 15.4.1`, ant-design-pro

Audited commit: `6f1acac` (`main`, "chore: fable-opus harness bookkeeping (p2f run closed: 6 units,
all adjudicated)"). **Read-only.** No pipeline run, no regeneration, no worktree, no git state
command. The only file written is this note; `git diff HEAD -- packages evidence` was empty before
it and is empty after it. Every number below was read off disk during this audit. Where a number
also appears in an existing note or on a board card, the disk reading is the one printed here.

**Verdict, stated once and not softened: `full_outcome_complete` is NOT declared, and this audit
does not declare it.** One conjunct of the oracle's second sentence holds strictly; the other
holds only in the widened sense, and the Angular half of the original ask is not demonstrable at
all. Detail in §6.

---

## 0. Audit integrity checks — VERBATIM, and they AGREE

would be this audit's headline. **None did.**

### 0d. Freeze composite — recomputed by hand from HEAD's own trees

`evidence/trust/current/adapter-freeze.json` publishes `freeze.composite`
`140ce86e163ddbae2ad6f1504022efca9468641cc50fd3dca354c6aba8cbb562`, over the preimage

**Exact match. The freeze is intact at HEAD and the composite is independently reproducible.** The
record names `supersedes.composite 27741d9c…` at commit `0ecd4106…` — supersession #1 (T010,
Angular-13 cell + format epoch) is landed and chain-recorded; `ADAPTER_FREEZE_COMMIT` is

moved (react for formatting alone, angular for both the 13-cell capability work and the format
epoch); three did not. **Supersession #2 has NOT been taken.** Its composite is unchanged from
the census, from the coverage report, and from HEAD.

**Headline of §0: there is no discrepancy to adjudicate.** Every published surface agrees with
what is on disk, and the freeze composite agrees with git.

---

## 1. Oracle half 1 — the command

> "In a clean checkout, a single command run against a real React or Angular application the
> pipeline has never handled completes unattended … and terminates in a coverage report that
> either records the app as newly proven or names a countable refusal reason."

### 1a. The current flame record — 9/9, count 0, and bounded

`evidence/runs/react-flame-v2-4-0/run-record.json` + `.interventions.json` at HEAD. **This is not
the T042 record**: flame was re-run three times today and the committed record is the third.

| field | value |
|---|---|
| `invocations` | `1` |
| `stdinReads` | `0` |
| `mutatedPathsOutsideWriteSet` | `[]` |
| `authoringPathsTouched` | `[]` |
| `interventionCount` | `0` |
| `exitCode` | `0` |
| `terminalClassification` | `proven` |
| `outcome` / `schema` | `proceeded` / `versionless.run.v1` |

Nine stages, all `ran`, with measured time:

```

ingest          32ms
license-at-pin   0ms   MIT, observed, "Copyright (c) 2021 Paweł Malak", LICENSE.md at the pin

build         1141ms   vite build -> build-vite, 24 output files, exit 0
witness       1437ms   synthesized-crawl, 1 journey, replayabilityRatio 1
```

**Bounded, in the row's own words** (`coverage-report.json`, `provenBoundedness`, derived from the
run record):

> "Dependency install scripts: the install row declares the install-script policy, names 3
> package(s) the lockfile marks as carrying an install script, and records npm starting 2
> script(s) and skipping 0 by policy. A script npm skipped did not run in the lane this proof was
> taken on."
>
> "Route reach: the witness row records the replay reaching 1 of 12 declared route(s) across 1
> journey(s). Every route it did not reach is unproven by this row rather than proven absent."

Two T042 residues are **closed** by this record: npm-12 `allowScripts` no longer silently blocks
(`flags: ["--foreground-scripts","--dangerously-allow-all-scripts"]`, 2 of 3 declared scripts
started, 0 skipped — where T042 read 3 declared and 0 started), and the shared
`evidence/runs/witness-synthesized/baseline/` slot is gone: the directory is now keyed per
application (`react-flame-v2-4-0/`, `react-coverview-a1470b01/`, `react-cra-redux-1a06509b/`,
`react-your-spotify-1-5-0/`, `react-papercups-v1-0-0/`, `angular-pigallery2-v1-7-0/`).

**Determinism at HEAD, threefold.** flame's three records today —
`pre-t047-run-record.json` (13:28), `pre-t048-run-record.json` (14:28), `run-record.json` (14:53)
— all read `proven`, `interventionCount 0`, and carry the **identical** witness digest
`35140e87ba151fb8fb466a8c680c8d33d0cf0af4737861526f8f5a4137a274ca`. The digest is stable across
two intervening code changes (T047, T048). It is *not* T042's `50b1e155…`: that digest was taken
in a different tree at a different commit, and the witness row's content has moved since (the
per-journey `outcomes` array is now published on the row). **Stability is demonstrated within a
code state, not across code states, and this audit claims only the former.**

### 1b. The three NEW proven records from today

All three ran as a single invocation each, `stdinReads 0`, `mutatedPathsOutsideWriteSet []`,
`authoringPathsTouched []`, `interventionCount 0`, `exitCode 0`, `terminalClassification proven`,
nine stages `ran`.

| app | repo @ pin | licence | 9/9 | count | witness digest | route reach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `react-coverview-a1470b01` | `rutikwankhade/CoverView` @ `a1470b01…` | MIT | yes | 0 | `8b8010cc…` | 1 of 4 |
| `react-cra-redux-1a06509b` | `notrab/create-react-app-redux` @ `1a06509b…` | MIT | yes | 0 | `28921dce…` | 1 of 4 |
| `react-your-spotify-1-5-0` | `Yooooomi/your_spotify` @ `50f6a0d8…` (tag 1.5.0) | **GPL-3.0** | yes | 0 | `39bdb50d…` | 1 of 5 |

Stage measurements read off the records:

```
coverview     install 14140ms  build 1581ms  vite build -> build-vite, 15 files  witness 2802ms
cra-redux     install 12423ms  build  976ms  vite build -> build-vite,  6 files  witness 2681ms
your-spotify  install 18264ms  build 2940ms  vite build -> build-vite, 17 files  witness 1144ms
```

**Through which policies** — the question that matters, because the policies are pre-declared
operator decisions and the T008 ruling permits them only as *recorded* decisions:

| app | `allowRemoteTarballs` | `allowInstallScripts` | `allowPeerConflicts` | `allowForeignLockfile` | `allowGitDependencies` | policy actually **exercised** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| flame | true | true | true | **false** | **false** | install-scripts (2 started) |
| coverview | true | true | true | true (declared) | true (declared) | install-scripts (1 started: `core-js-pure@3.49.0` postinstall); **git dependency fetched**: `file-saver@git+ssh://git@github.com/eligrey/FileSaver.js.git#e865e37a…` |
| cra-redux | true | true | true | **true (used)** | true (declared) | **foreign lockfile**: `yarn.lock` present, `consulted: false` |
| your-spotify | true | true | true | **true (used)** | true (declared) | **foreign lockfile**: `yarn.lock` present, `consulted: false` |

The distinction between *declared* and *exercised* is not cosmetic. `foreignLockfileDisregarded`
is `null` on flame and coverview (npm lockfiles; nothing to disregard) and populated on the other
two, verbatim:

> "The allow-foreign-lockfile policy was declared, so this install proceeded without the closure
> yarn pinned in `yarn.lock`: the file was left on disk untouched and was not consulted, and npm
> resolved every dependency fresh from the lane manifest instead. This resolution is NOT pinned by
> the era lockfile, so the installed closure may drift from the one the era application shipped
> with, and every claim downstream of this install is bounded by that drift."

**Two of the fourteen proven rows stand on that policy.** See §2f — it is one of the two live
owner questions with a number attached.

One further reading worth carrying, from your-spotify's build row (the T047 fix, in the record's
own words): the era-cell stage `provisioned` `node-16` from `Dockerfile#FROM line 1`
(`node:16-alpine` → `v16.20.2` at
`.versionless/cache/angular-13-cell-runtime/node-v16.20.2-darwin-arm64`), and the build stage then
recorded that reading under `eraDeclared` while running the *migrated* lane on the runtime its
target requires (`v24.15.0`) — "Both readings are true and they are about different trees."

### 1c. "Unseen app" — what evidence exists, precisely

The oracle says *never handled*. Read strictly, that phrase was satisfied once, at T042, and today
adds a different and arguably harder kind of evidence.

- **flame** — the clean-checkout proof. T042 (sealed, commit `d9cd48e`) acquired it fresh into a
  `git worktree add <tmp> HEAD` and ran the harness twice at count 0 with identical digests. That
  is the only *clean-checkout, never-handled* run on the record, and this audit does not re-run it.
  Today's three flame runs are working-tree re-runs of an app the pipeline had already proven.
- **coverview** — first handled 2026-08-17 (`t029-install-defect-run-record.json`,
  `defect:install`, count 0). Today: `proven`. Never previously proven.
- **cra-redux** — first handled 2026-08-17 (`t030-lockfile-foreign-run-record.json`,
  `refused:install.lockfile-foreign`, count 0). Today: `proven`. Never previously proven.
- **your-spotify** — first handled 2026-08-17 (`t030-…`, same named refusal, count 0), then twice
  today at `defect:build` (`pre-t047`: "You are using Node.js 16.20.2. Vite requires Node.js
  version 20.19+"; `pre-t048`: "Tsconfig not found `<lane-parent>/tsconfig.json`"), then `proven`
  on the third attempt at 14:54. Every one of the four attempts was a single invocation at count 0.

**The honest statement: none of today's three was a first-contact run.** All three were apps the
pipeline had previously **refused or defected on by name**, and all three crossed after the wall
that named them was removed (`--allow-foreign-lockfile` in T043-b, target-runtime semantics in
T047, tsconfig travel in T048). That is exactly the loop the charter designed — "every app either
raises proven coverage or emits a named, countable, honest refusal that becomes the next admission
backlog item" — and today it closed three times in one day. It is *not* additional evidence that
an unseen app works first time; the only evidence for that remains flame at T042, n = 1.

### 1d. What this audit does NOT re-verify

- **Nothing was run through the pipeline.** No `run`, no `acquire`, no `batch`, no regeneration.
- **The clean-checkout gate is not re-executed here.** Its standing proof is T042's sealed result
  (`notes/T042-reaudit.md` §1, at commit `d9cd48e`): fresh worktree, `pnpm install
  --frozen-lockfile`, consented acquire reproducing the committed pin on every content field,
  harness twice at count 0 with identical `50b1e155…` digests, and a named refusal
  (`refused:apply.lane-already-carries-files`) on a literal same-lane repeat.
- **Today's four proven runs were taken in the working tree**, not in a clean checkout. Their
  intervention records name the lanes under the session scratchpad; `trackedPathsSource: git`.
- **`npm run build` is still a precondition of verification in a pristine checkout** (T042 §1d:
  `dist/` is gitignored and a provenance subject). This audit ran the checks in a tree that
  already carries a built `dist`, so it does not re-test that path. T032 delivered
  `trust.distribution-not-built` as a named refusal with a runbook line; that this audit's §0
  passed says nothing about the pristine case either way.
- **The count is what the harness can see from outside.** Its own `notEstablished` is unchanged
  and still binds: `node_modules` and `.git` are not walked below the roots; identical rewrites,
  permission changes and symlink retargets are not counted; `stdinReads: 0` is a construction
  (stdin `ignore`, `CI=1`), not a syscall measurement.

**Half-1 reading at HEAD: the command works, unattended, at a measured zero, on four independent
React applications, and refuses by name when it cannot proceed. The clean-checkout, never-handled
conjunct rests on one sealed run (flame/T042) and has not been widened since.**

---

## 2. Oracle half 2 — coverage and capability above the sealed baseline

> "Run repeatedly, that command raises the proven-app count **and** capability matrix above the
> sealed baseline."

### 2a. Totals, read off `evidence/trust/current/coverage-report.json`

```
totals = {"applications":29,"proven":14,"bounded":2,"refused":7,"not-admitted":6}
```

Sealed baseline as the report itself publishes it (`sealedBaseline`): `angular {ready 4, total 4}`,
`react {ready 6, total 6}` — **10 sealed proven** — plus `capabilities {total 59, crossProven 8,
experimental 51, crossProvenThreshold 2}`. The baseline the goal was opened against was **proven
10 / 8-of-58 capabilities**; the denominator has since grown to 59 (T010 u7: one new
`locale-id-provider` capability; `crossProven` unmoved at 8).

Movement across the goal: **proven 10 → 11 (T042) → 14 (today). Applications 21 → 29.**

### 2b. The four proven-by-derivation rows

Each carries `provenanceOfStatus: run-record`, `interventionCount 0`, a nine-row stage table all
`ran`, a `source` block with repository/ref/revision/licence identifier + licence sha256, a
`basisPath` naming its run record, and derived `provenBoundedness`:

|---|---|---|
| `react-coverview-a1470b01` | `evidence/runs/react-coverview-a1470b01/run-record.json` | `24ae4dee…` |
| `react-cra-redux-1a06509b` | `evidence/runs/react-cra-redux-1a06509b/run-record.json` | `b2675162…` |
| `react-flame-v2-4-0` | `evidence/runs/react-flame-v2-4-0/run-record.json` | `fbfe1067…` |
| `react-your-spotify-1-5-0` | `evidence/runs/react-your-spotify-1-5-0/run-record.json` | `230184f6…` |

T042's two open flame items are closed: the row now carries `framework: "react"` and a full source
block. The rule that admits them is published on the report itself (`interventionRule.applied:
true`) and is the T027 bar verbatim — run record exists, `interventions.count === 0`, and **every**
stage row reads `ran`; an unasserted count is "not a measured zero".

**All four are React.** No Angular application has ever been recorded proven from a run record.

### 2c. Every non-proven row, with its code

`refused` — 7 rows, 7 **distinct** codes, one each:

|---|---|
| `plan.lineage-no-frozen-adapter-claims` | `next-tailwind-starter-blog` |

  "applicationFilesChanged=0 … a dependency version bump rebuilt under AOT rather than a proven

`bounded` — 2 rows, strings quoted verbatim and not restated anywhere in the package: `passed`
(cypress-rwa holdout) and `witness-passed-on-bounded-anonymous-catalog-surface` (eShop holdout).

**Every non-proven row is legible: a named code or a named defect classification, at intervention

The five `defect` rows are the Angular/React walls measured today, and they are the gap map's

### 2d. Capabilities — 8 / 51 / 59, and the one derived proof

`evidence/trust/current/capability-coverage.json` `summary`:


`react-cra-vite-adapter`, and it cites **four** of them —
`evidence/runs/{react-coverview-a1470b01,react-cra-redux-1a06509b,react-flame-v2-4-0,react-your-spotify-1-5-0}/run-record.json`.
(A prior framing of this audit's brief described the derived proof as "flame"; on disk at HEAD it
is four run records on that one capability. The published record is self-consistent; the summary
was stale. This is a correction to a note, not a discrepancy in the evidence.) Its own published
note says so:

> "create-react-app to Vite 8 adapter; fired on three independent create-react-app applications at
> the seal. Cross-proven in adapter-freeze. Three is the sealed figure and not the published one:
> an application past those three was derived from a `versionless run` record admitted after the
> seal, and is cited by that record rather than by a fixture."

### 2e. Verdict, per conjunct

- **Proven-app count: STRICTLY ABOVE the baseline.** 14 vs 10 sealed, +4, every one of the four
  derived from a run record rather than hand-entered, every one re-derivable
  (`report:coverage --verify-only` = `mode: verified`). **This conjunct holds.**

  by one new capability published under the authorized T010 supersession, and (ii) the *depth* of

  of them derived from run records. **No capability crossed the threshold of 2 that had not
  already crossed it.** Read as "the 59-capability cross-proof ledger", the conjunct does NOT hold.

unchanged from T042 §2: T024 + T025 (the matrix cannot move while `provenApps` are string literals
in `capability-coverage.ts`), fed by an Angular grind that cannot start until §3(a) is ruled — or
an owner decision recording which of the two readings of "capability matrix" was meant. That
re-reading should be an owner decision, not a board assumption.

### 2f. What the 14 depends on — two live owner questions, priced

This is the part a bank's auditor would ask about, so it is stated with numbers.

1. **Foreign lockfile.** 2 of the 14 proven rows (`cra-redux`, `your-spotify`) reached `proven`

   Both were previously `refused:install.lockfile-foreign` and both crossed only after the policy
   shipped. If the owner rules that a proven row may **not** be reached that way, proven falls
